idiom_name: SimpleDelegator subclass for the old object shape + explicit Hash mapping
implementation_notes: The standard library's delegate gives Ruby a ready-made forwarding object - SimpleDelegator 'provides the means to delegate all supported method calls to the object passed into the constructor' - so the window can present the legacy object with its old method names while the modernized implementation sits behind it; Forwardable is the variant when only selected names should be forwarded. The payload half stays explicit: two methods that build and parse the legacy Hash (or the old XML with REXML or Nokogiri) are the actual contract, and no delegation helper can derive them. The hand-written class is still justified when the legacy surface also fixes arity, naming conventions or block behaviour, which delegation alone does not promise.
code_sketch:
require 'delegate'

class LegacyQuote < SimpleDelegator        # frozen legacy object shape
  def initialize(quote) = super(quote)     # delegates to the new domain object
  def SKU = __getobj__.sku                 # old, capitalised reader names
  def unit_price = format('%.2f', __getobj__.cents / 100.0)  # text decimal
  def ccy = __getobj__.currency || 'EUR'   # default is part of the contract
end

# window entry point: one place that knows the old payload shape
def to_legacy(quote) = { 'SKU' => quote.sku, 'unit_price' => format('%.2f', quote.cents / 100.0) }
pitfalls: Delegation answers to names the legacy object never had, so respond_to? and instance_of? checks in old callers can start behaving differently.
Formatting money through floats reintroduces rounding; keep cents as Integer or BigDecimal and convert only at the edge.
Gems that monkey-patch core classes change what a generic to_h serialises, which is why the frozen shape needs its own explicit Hash.
